question: Should exact requester consumption count as terminal descendant delivery even when the requester’s eventual outward delivery fails?
rationale: The patch deliberately equates internal consumption with `delivered`, which changes retry, cleanup, persisted state, detached-task projection, and downstream progress semantics; tests cannot decide that product contract.

options.title: Accept Consumption As Delivery
options.body: Treat exact requester consumption as terminal descendant delivery, then require exact-head live and restart proof before merge.

options.title: Separate Consumption From Delivery
options.body: Persist a distinct consumed-by-requester state and let cleanup use it without reporting external delivery as successful.

options.title: Fold Into Durable Inbox
options.body: Pause this PR and resolve consumption, retry, and outward-delivery semantics in the broader durable completion inbox design.

recommendation.title: Accept Consumption As Delivery
recommendation.body: Treat exact requester consumption as terminal descendant delivery, then require exact-head live and restart proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest recent-history routing candidate across the affected cron, lifecycle, and persisted registry surfaces.
